what: Forecast of the prepared H100 run (docs/PLAN_V5_FROM_SCRATCH.md §11, Nachtrag 16. Oktober): four independent estimates, three critiques, one revision (read-only analysis, 16 Oct 2026). Estimates, not measurements; the run itself decides.
inputs_note: Besides val-A and published references the estimates used existing CPU evaluations on the test split split by source (GPT-2 small on filtered vs. kept C4 test documents), only to estimate the effect of the extended filter. No change was chosen by test scores.

final.training_tokens_expected:
Median about 4.6 B tokens for a normal H100 SXM run (about 4.5 B across all runs; p10 about 3.4 B, p90 about 5.7 B), about 0.7 passes over the 6.44 B-token train_all.

Timeline:
- Throughput about 300 k tok/s (range 260-345 k).
- Setup before the main run about 70-75 min: checks, base data, the sweep running alongside the 36-shard preparation, merge, contamination check.
- The main window is then about 6.23 - 1.2 - 0.5 = 4.5 h. At step 100 the run fits 0.95 x the time left, which is about 4.25 h of actual training.
- After that: about 13 min of unused margin, then the 30-min reserve.

Sensitivity:
- At 270 k tok/s it is about 4.2 B tokens; at 330 k about 5.0 B.
- Each ±10 % of tokens moves the forecast by about ∓0.003 bpb.
- The step-100 log line fixes the count.

Tails:
- About 10 % chance of a degraded run at 0.55-0.85x tokens: an NVL or PCIe card billed against the fixed 4.01 $/h, an eager fallback, or slow downloads.
- About 2 % chance the decay is cut short by a later slowdown.

WikiText is about 1.75 % of the stream, so about 80 M WikiText tokens are seen.

Price: the RunPod price page (16 Oct 2026) shows Secure SXM at 3.99 $/h, so H100_PRICE 4.01 (about 3.99 plus storage) is correct for the planned card. There is no hidden headroom.
final.reasoning:
WHAT I RE-CHECKED (read-only; small numpy only)

h100_train.py:
- doc_mask builds a dense (B,1,T,T) mask, so SDPA cannot use flash.
- loss_sum += float(loss.detach()) runs after every one of the 16 micro-batches (line 393), and each batch is pinned with a fresh pin_memory() (line 384).
- The exception fallback only applies within 3 steps of a start (`meta["step"] > start_step + 3` → raise).
- The token budget is fitted once, at step 100, with a 0.95 margin. Training is cut 15 min after the deadline.
- The sweep defaults are 1e-3/2e-3/4e-3 at 200 M tokens with 100 warmup steps. Within 0.003 bpb the smaller rate wins.
- --budget-hours defaults to 5.5. h100_run.sh sets RESERVE_S=1800 and PRICE 4.01.

Data and filter:
- Base train has 29,245 WikiText docs interleaved among 383,085 (52,972 source switches), so a WikiText upweight must select documents via train.keys.jsonl.
- The extended-filter shard-1 probe list was not saved, and the repo has no timing record for shard 1.
- The running CPU extension is `experiments.v5_long train`, started by v5_long_ext_run.sh. It re-imports v5_long.py when it restarts, so H100-only changes must not touch v5_long.py.

Machine:
- The root disk has 273 MB free (100 % full). Any local test must write to /dev/shm.

Literature, verified:
- RunPod pricing (https://www.runpod.io/pricing, fetched 16 Oct 2026):
  - Secure Cloud: H100 SXM 3.99, NVL 3.19, PCIe 2.89 $/h.
  - Community Cloud: H100 SXM 2.69, NVL 2.59, PCIe 1.99 $/h.
- Bjorck et al. (https://arxiv.org/html/2409.19913v3), Table 5: β = 0.653 for 125M models at 0.5M-token batches. The 0.32 transfer rule is recommended only for models of 760M and up.
- modded-nanogpt AdamW record (https://github.com/KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt/tree/master/records/track_1_short/2024-06-06_AdamW): "batch size 2^19, so ~5B tokens", lr 0.0018, warmup 250, warmdown 2000, betas (0.9, 0.95), marked IIRC. The README does not state the attention implementation or the timing.
- UNVERIFIED: the GPT-2 checkpoint scoring about 3.29 on FineWeb.

CRITIQUE POINTS ACCEPTED
1. Extended filter, from critique 1. Verified: the 40 C4 test docs already excluded score 1.040 for GPT-2, against 1.072 for kept C4. Length-matched kept docs are harder: <500 B 1.360 kept vs 1.341 excluded; 500-1000 B 1.168 vs 1.085. So near-duplicate template pages are easy, and the synthesis's -0.002 credit has no support. I use N(0, 0.004), which shifts the median by about +0.002.
2. Batch efficiency, raised by both critique 1 and critique 2. Going from 8 k to 524 k tokens per step, with E/Emin = 1 + B/Bcrit and Bcrit of a few hundred k to about 0.7 M, gives about 0.55-0.7. I use U(0.55, 0.95) instead of U(0.65, 1.05) in the internal anchor: about +0.0016.
3. Throughput and setup, partly accepted.
   - Best PyTorch reference: modded-nanogpt record #2 at about 332 k tok/s per H100, with causal flash and V = 50304 tied.
   - Our smaller head saves about 8 ms per 32 k tokens. The dense-mask memory-efficient kernel costs about +12-20 ms. The per-micro-batch sync costs about 1-3 %.
   - Net about 300 k (range 260-345 k), not 315 k (synthesis) nor 270 k (critique 1).
   - Critique 2's 330-380 k rests on llm.c (hand-written CUDA), which is not a valid reference for this code.
   - Setup about 72 min.
   - Combined: median tokens 4.8 → 4.6 B, about +0.0015.
4. Learning-rate penalty in the internal anchor x0.6 (critique 2). The CPU learning rate also came from a 45-min sweep at about a 5 M-token horizon: about -0.0004.
5. Size effect, partly accepted: U(0.014, 0.036), about -0.0006. Chinchilla on total parameters gives about 0.023-0.025 bpb.
6. Wiki/C4 ratio r: the critiques pull in opposite directions, so I widen it to N(0.932, 0.015) without moving the centre.
7. Context credit widened to U(0.002, 0.010). Verified: the CPU model's C4 ratio to GPT-2 rises with document length (1.034 for <500 B docs, 1.144 for >5 KB), and the H100 trains at 1024 throughout: about -0.001.
8. Degraded-branch probability 12 → 10 %, plus a 2 % truncated-decay branch. Those two roughly cancel.
9. Critique 2's double-counting arithmetic in the text path is right. Combined with undoing the filter credit, the text path comes to about 1.039.
10. Critique 3's arithmetic slip is right: a median of 1.028 with sd 0.028 gives P about 0.64, not 0.68.

CRITIQUE POINTS REJECTED
- Critique 2's 3.49 $/h price: the live page says 3.99.
- Critique 2's repetition credit: the anchor already discounts epoch-2 tokens with kap U(0.2, 0.7).
- Both moves of the tokens-to-parity anchor (critique 1: 4.3-4.6 B; critique 2: 3.5 B): the RoPE fact cuts both ways (the record already includes RoPE, while QK-norm, ReLU², untied head and softcap are extra credit), and our recipe is untuned beyond the learning rate. I keep lognormal(3.9 B, 0.45).
- Critique 1's full +0.008 shift: several of its components are smaller once checked.

RESULT
- The revised Monte Carlo ((local scratch script, not kept), scen.py; 300 k draws; stable across seeds) gives p10 1.009, median 1.042, p90 1.075, P(≤1.04 | valid result) = 0.467.
- The internal anchor alone gives 1.045; the external anchor alone 1.040.
- Blending with the text path (about 1.039) gives median 1.041, p10 1.008, p90 1.075.
- P is about 0.48 if a valid result exists and about 0.46 after a 4 % chance of no valid result.
- With every recommended change below: median about 1.030, P about 0.62-0.63. Without FlexAttention: about 1.035, P about 0.55.

CALIBRATION CHECKPOINTS
- The step-100 throughput and token-budget line.
- The curve on the 150 C4-only val-A docs at 0.5 and 1.0 B tokens.
- long_ext1 will not report in time: 492.6 → 506.2 M tokens in 6 h is about 2.3 M tok/h, so the remaining about 634 M tokens take about 11-12 days.

OPERATIONAL NOTE
The full root disk may be making long_ext1's disk checkpoints fail (the PLAN §10 failure mode).
disagreements: Throughput. Critique 1 says 250-290 k tok/s (central 270 k), critique 2 says 330-380 k, the synthesis 315 k. I resolved it at about 300 k (range 260-345 k). The anchor is modded-nanogpt record #2, about 332 k tok/s per H100 with causal flash. Against it: the dense-mask memory-efficient kernel costs about +12-20 ms per 32 k tokens, the 32 k untied head saves about 8 ms, and the per-micro-batch float(loss) sync costs 1-3 %. llm.c's 463 k is hand-written CUDA and not a reference for this PyTorch path. Median tokens move to about 4.6 B.

Extended filter. I accepted critique 1 over the synthesis and D. Verified from models/lm/gpt2/eval_test.json and results/lm/dedup.json: the 40 already-excluded C4 near-duplicates score 1.040 for GPT-2, against 1.072 for kept C4. Length-matched kept docs are harder (<500 B: 1.360 vs 1.341; 500-1000 B: 1.168 vs 1.085). The -0.002 credit becomes 0 ± 0.004.
Batch efficiency in the internal anchor. Both critique 1 and critique 2 call U(0.65, 1.05) optimistic for 8 k → 524 k tokens per step (E/Emin = 1 + B/Bcrit). Changed to U(0.55, 0.95).

Tokens to C4 parity in the external anchor. Critique 1 says 4.3-4.6 B, critique 2 says 3.5 B. Kept at lognormal(3.9 B, 0.45). Record #2 already includes RoPE (critique 1 is right on that), but our QK-norm, ReLU², untied head and softcap are extra credit (critique 2), and our recipe is only tuned on the learning rate. The arguments roughly cancel.
Wiki/C4 ratio r. Critique 1 wants 0.93-0.95, critique 2 wants N(0.928, 0.016). Kept the centre at 0.932 and widened sd to 0.015. Neither direction has a measurement of a C4-dominant model behind it.

Price lever. Critique 2's 3.49 $/h is rejected. runpod.io/pricing (16 Oct 2026) shows Secure SXM 3.99 (so 4.01 including storage is correct), NVL 3.19, PCIe 2.89, Community SXM 2.69 (critique 3 verified). Setting the true price gains nothing on the planned Secure SXM card. It only removes the degraded branch for NVL/PCIe, and only if H100_BUDGET_HOURS is raised too, because the 5.5-h cap binds below about 3.45 $/h.

Learning-rate rule. Switched from D's cap-only rule to critique 3's band rule: winner x 0.5, clipped to [1e-3, 2e-3]. Bjorck et al. Table 5 (verified) gives β = 0.653 for 125M at 0.5M-token batches; even β = 0.32 implies x0.37 for a 23x horizon. The floor and cap keep the rate inside the band supported by modded-nanogpt's 1.8e-3 (IIRC) and the CPU recipe. The two rules differ by about ±0.002 bpb.

Size effect. Critique 2 wants U(0.018, 0.036). Partly accepted as U(0.014, 0.036): Chinchilla on total parameters gives about 0.023-0.025 bpb, and nothing ties its size coefficient to our measured data slope.
Repetition and restart credit for the CPU baseline (critique 2). Rejected for repetition: the internal anchor already discounts second-epoch tokens (kap U(0.2, 0.7)). Restarts are negligible.

Size of the median shift. Critique 1 suggests 1.045 / P 0.40, critique 2 1.033 / 0.58, critique 3 1.037 / 0.53. My revision is 1.041 / 0.46. It moves toward critique 1 on the verified filter evidence and the batch-efficiency point, but by less than critique 1 proposes, because its throughput (270 k) and parity (4.3-4.6 B) inputs do not survive checking.

Probability for the improved case (critique 3): the synthesis's 0.68 for a median of 1.028 was an arithmetic slip (correct value about 0.64). Recomputed with the Monte Carlo for the full revised package: median about 1.030, P about 0.62-0.63.

ranked_improvements.change: Block-sparse training attention: FlexAttention with a causal AND same-document BlockMask, with hardened guards. (a) Implement it only in h100_train.py, as a patched or subclassed Block, never in v5_long.py: the running CPU extension re-imports v5_long.py on every restart. (b) Gate on torch ≥2.6. (c) Build the block mask on the GPU per micro-batch with create_block_mask(..., _compile=True), and wrap flex_attention in its own torch.compile(dynamic=False) so a recompile limit cannot silently drop to the slow eager path. (d) At startup, compare loss and grad norm on one batch against the dense path, time about 10 steps of each, and use Flex only if it is equivalent and at least 10 % faster. (e) On an exception at ANY step, switch to the existing dense path instead of exiting with code 1. Persist a 'flex disabled' flag in the state or meta so restarts do not retry Flex. (f) Leave the eval path untouched. (g) Check mask equivalence on the local CPU in eager mode with a tiny model, writing only to /dev/shm (the root disk is full). Re-pin the guide's commit and redo the smoke test and the review. Keep the is_causal flash path without the document mask only as a last resort: it changes the recipe.
ranked_improvements.expected_gain_bpb: -0.006 central (-0.004 to -0.010); +15-30 % throughput (critique 3's packing simulation: 42 % of 128x128 blocks active vs 100 % now); P(stage 1) about +8-9 points
ranked_improvements.risk: Medium-low with guards (a)-(g) plus the periodic re-fit below. The GPU path cannot be exercised by the CPU smoke test. Every failure mode ends on the unchanged dense path at a cost of minutes. A mask bug can only hurt training, never inflate the score.
ranked_improvements.cost: About 1 day of development plus re-review and a re-pinned guide commit. About 2 min of pod time for the check. A cheap-GPU dry run is optional and comes out of the same 30 $ credit.
ranked_improvements.why: The largest code lever on tokens, which drive the forecast. The dense mask forces the memory-efficient kernel over the full T^2. Recommended only with the hardened guards, so it cannot cause a FEHLER or a silent throughput collapse in the paid run.

forecasts.method:
Method A, using only our own measurements. I anchored on the final CPU evaluation and extrapolated each part of the test set separately with a local data-scaling slope taken from our own curve, then propagated the uncertainty with a Monte Carlo (400k draws, script at (local scratch script, not kept)).

(1) Split the test score by source. The filtered test set is 59.0% C4 and 41.0% WikiText by bytes. Our 600M-token model scores C4 1.1913 and wiki 1.0695; GPT-2 scores C4 1.0723 and wiki 0.9905. This matters because the H100 data adds only C4: the wiki share of training text falls from 40% to 1.8%.

(2) Handle the 150-document curve. The first 150 val-A documents are all C4, so the curve measures C4 only. At 600M tokens the offset to test-C4 is additive: 1.2402 on the curve versus 1.1913 (difference -0.049). This offset drifts only from -0.038/-0.043 in the short runs to -0.049, so I used the curve's slope and the final eval's level.

(3) Data slope. The C4 bpb drop per doubling of tokens at about 355M tokens is set to N(0.055, 0.012). Sources: the curve during constant learning rate at context 1024 (0.062±0.021), the training loss over 300-420M (0.052±0.027), the training loss over 160-285M, and two context-512-phase estimates that are biased in opposite directions (0.039 low, 0.058 high). I multiplied by 1.03 because the slope was measured on repeated (epoch-2) data, then moved it to the end of the CPU run as slope × (600/355)^-beta.

(4) Extrapolation form: bpb change = s/(beta·ln2)·(k^-beta - 1), where k is the ratio of effective tokens.
- C4 effective tokens = C4 tokens + kappa·wiki tokens, kappa ~ U(0.2, 0.7).
- Wiki effective tokens = wiki tokens + kappa_w·C4 tokens, kappa_w ~ U(0.05, 0.5); wiki slope = C4 slope × U(0.8, 1.25).
- beta ~ U(0.15, 0.45).
- Batch and recipe efficiency of the H100 run relative to the CPU run (8k vs 524k tokens per step, beta2, learning rate, context): m_B ~ U(0.65, 1.10).
- Model size 59M → 85M body parameters: Chinchilla-style balance prior (ratio of returns from size versus data 0.4-1.0, size exponent 0.25-0.45), giving -0.01 to -0.03.
- Recipe noise sd 0.012, extended-filter effect 0 ± 0.006, seed noise 0.004, structural sd 0.015.
- H100 training tokens: lognormal, plus a 12% chance of a degraded run (slower GPU or eager/chunked fallback) at 0.5-0.8× the tokens.

(5) Cross-check from the literature (not part of the fit): this lands the model at about GPT-2 level on C4 (1.066 vs 1.072) and on wiki (0.987 vs 0.99). That is consistent with speedrun-style evidence that a modern AdamW 124M model needs about 4-7B in-distribution tokens to match GPT-2.

Poorly constrained, in order of impact: the data slope (correlation with the result -0.71), beta, the size effect (our data has no clean model-size variation at a matched recipe), C4-to-wiki transfer (kappa_w), batch efficiency (m_B), and H100 throughput (never measured). The anchor and the C4/wiki split are well constrained.

The forecast is conditional on the run completing. With about 5% risk of no valid result, the unconditional probability is about 0.54.

Considered but not listed as improvements:
- Lowering the learning rate for the longer horizon. Bjorck et al. suggest the 200M-token sweep could be up to about 2.8× too high, but the sign and size are unverified for a 381-step sweep.
- A bigger or deeper model: no more than about 0.01 gain, and the size effect is unconstrained by our data.
- Changing the decay shape: no more than about 0.003.
forecasts.tokens: Prepared plan: about 4.8B tokens median (p10 about 3.4B, p90 about 6.8B; capped at 10B). Basis: 25 USD / 4.01 = 6.23 h of pod time, minus the 0.5 h reserve, minus about 1.1-1.4 h of checks, base data, sweep alongside the 36-shard download and tokenisation, merge and contamination check, leaves about 4.3-4.6 h of training. Throughput assumed 300-420k tokens/s, times the 0.95 fit factor. The rate is held down by attention: v5_long.Block calls SDPA with a dense (B,1,1024,1024) boolean document mask, so FlashAttention is never used and the full T² is computed. For comparison, llm.c on 8×H100 managed about 463k tokens/s per GPU (10B tokens in 45 min; my arithmetic). The plan's own number, 6B tokens in 5.5 h, implies about 300k tokens/s. In the Monte Carlo the median is 4.8B and 6% more tokens shifts the median by about -0.003 bpb.

forecasts.method:
Method B (literature anchors), cross-checked against our own CPU model. Nothing was trained and no repo files were changed. The only computations were small numpy calculations on JSON/NPY files plus a Monte Carlo in the scratchpad ((local scratch script, not kept)).

(1) Token budget. 25 USD / 4.01 USD/h = 6.23 h of pod time. Before training, about 80 min go to user steps, base data, and the 3x200M-token sweep (which overlaps the 36-shard C4 preparation), then merge and contamination check. The script also keeps a 30-min reserve. That leaves about 4.1-4.4 h of training. Throughput is taken as 300-350k tok/s: the plan's own 6B tokens in 5.5 h implies 303k tok/s; llm.c's highly optimised CUDA code runs about 463k tok/s per H100; our PyTorch path uses a dense boolean doc mask, so SDPA cannot use the flash kernel. Result: about 4.6B tokens.

(2) Path L (literature, tokens to reach GPT-2 parity on web text the model was trained on). On FineWeb, llm.c's GPT-2-recipe 124M model (AdamW, 0.5M batch) roughly matches or slightly beats the OpenAI checkpoint after about 10B tokens: val 3.28-3.29, HellaSwag 29.9 vs 29.4. Loss parity probably arrives earlier, around 5-9B tokens. A tuned LR plus rotary embeddings is about 1.4-2x more token-efficient (modded-nanogpt record #2), and our fast-v1 recipe has further modern tweaks. So our recipe should reach parity at T* of about 2.4-6B tokens (median about 3.8B). With a local slope of about 3% per doubling, at 4.6B the C4 part of our test comes out at about 0.99x GPT-2.

(3) Path A (anchor on our own CPU model, per domain). The 59M CPU model scores 1.191 on the C4 test docs (GPT-2 1.072) and 1.0695 on the wiki docs (GPT-2 0.9905). I scaled each domain by its effective data. The CPU run's 8k-token batch is taken as worth 1.2-1.3x as much per token as 524k (Zhang et al. critical batch size of about 0.5-0.6M tokens). For the wiki domain, C4 tokens count partially through transfer, because the H100 mix is only 1.8% WikiText against 40% in the base corpus the test comes from. I used 2.5-3.5% gain per doubling: our C4-only val-A curve measures 3.6% per doubling at 0.3B tokens, consistent with Kaplan-type curvature. Body size 59M to 85M adds about -2.4%, and full 1024 context from the start adds about -0.5%. Result: about 1.010-1.038, centre 1.024.

(4) Tails. A literal Chinchilla fit (Hoffmann or Epoch) predicts about 0.93, but its data slope is twice what we measured, so it gets little weight. A Kaplan form calibrated to our slope predicts about 1.06 with little headroom even at infinite data; nanoGPT's 3.12 to 2.85 on OWT contradicts that, so it gets 15% weight. I add +0.004 for the 200M-token sweep probably picking too high an LR for a 23x longer run (Bjorck et al.: optimal LR scales as D^-0.65 at 125M).

(5) Blend. Centre 1.038 for a run without failures, method sd 0.028. Monte Carlo adds token-count uncertainty, seed noise, a possible ±0.004 shift of the GPT-2 reference under the extended filter, a 12% chance of a degraded run (+0.005 to +0.03) and a 3% chance of no valid result. Each 0.01 bpb of improvement is worth about +12 percentage points of P(stage 1).
forecasts.tokens: Median 4.6B tokens (p10 3.5B, p90 6.0B) at 524,288 tokens/step: about 4.1-4.4 h of main training at 300-350k tok/s on one H100 SXM, after about 80 min of preparation and a 30-min reserve inside 6.23 h of pod time. The training stream is base (285M) + C4 shards 1-36 (about 6.15B) = about 6.44B tokens, so about 0.7 of it is seen once. WikiText-103 is about 1.8% of training tokens (about 75M wiki tokens seen, against 238M in the CPU run).

forecasts.method: Method C, a realistic token count. Step 1: I read h100_run.sh, h100_train.py, h100_data.py, h100_meter.sh and H100_ANLEITUNG.md and rebuilt the time line under the brake: 25 USD / 4.01 USD/h = 6.234 h (374 min). Training must end by billed time minus the 30 min RESERVE_S, i.e. at 344 min. At step 100 the trainer resizes its token budget to 0.95 x the time left at the measured rate. Billed time per phase, central (p10-p90): pod start plus the user's commands 6 min; checks and packages 2-3 min; base data 11 min (8-15); stage 3 = max(sweep 3x200M at ~330k tok/s = 30 min + compile ~3 min, extra data: 36 C4 shards of 318 MB at ~50 s each = ~31 min) ~36 min; merge of 12.9 GB 2 min; contamination scan of 6.44B tokens 3 min; stream build over 13.2M docs plus compile 3 min. Main training therefore starts at about 64 min (55-75) and has about 4.4 h (4.26-4.58 h) at the measured rate. It ends about 10 min before the deadline. Final eval (fp32, ~2.0M tokens, under 1 min), samples, the upload of 0.54 + 1.6 GB, the 2-min sleep and termination use about 10 min. About 25-30 min (~1.9 USD) of the budget goes unused. Step 2, throughput as implemented: bf16 autocast yes; torch.compile yes (model.hidden plus the fused soft-capped loss, which materialises 32768x32768 logits); micro-batch 32x1024 with 16 accumulation steps; fused AdamW; one sync per micro-batch (float(loss), under 1%). Attention is the weak point. doc_mask builds a dense boolean (B,1,T,T) mask, so SDPA cannot use FlashAttention or skip the causal half. It falls back to the memory-efficient kernel computing full T^2: about 25-40 ms per 32k tokens, against about 7 ms for causal flash. Per 32k-token micro-batch I estimate matmuls about 36 ms (21.7 TFLOP at ~600 TFLOPS), attention about 32 ms, fused elementwise about 15 ms, loss about 6 ms: roughly 90-100 ms, so about 330-350k tok/s. Public references: llm.c 468k tok/s per H100; Keller Jordan's PyTorch AdamW baseline 332k; ModernArch 366k. I added a 7% chance of the eager/chunked fallback (x0.62) and an 8% chance of a non-SXM GPU (x0.78). Monte Carlo result: R p10/p50/p90 = 236k/328k/432k tok/s; main-training tokens D = 3.6/5.25/7.0 B. Step 3, from tokens to bpb: bpb = 1.039 + s*log2(P/D) + eps, where P is the token count at which this recipe reaches GPT-2 parity on these documents. P: median 4.0B, sigma_ln 0.5; s: 0.020-0.035 bpb per doubling; eps: N(+0.002, 0.008) for LR choice, seed and filter shift. Two anchors set P. External: the modded-nanogpt AdamW baseline (rotary, LR 1.8e-3, 2^19 batch) matched llm.c's 10B-token loss in about 5B tokens. llm.c at 10B beats the OpenAI checkpoint on FineWeb. fast-v1's QK-norm, ReLU^2, zero-init and untied head are worth about 1.2-1.35x, so P is about 2.5-3.8B. Internal: extrapolating the CPU run (1.141 at 0.6B; about -0.046 bpb per doubling, shrinking as D^-0.3) with a 0.55-0.8 token haircut for batch 524k vs 8k gives about 1.02-1.045 at 5.25B, so P is about 3.5-5.5B. The test is 59% C4 / 41% WikiText by bytes. GPT-2 (no Wikipedia in training) scores 1.072 on the C4 part and 0.990 on wiki. The H100 mix is about 98% C4 and 2% Wikipedia. So parity on the mix is about parity on C4. Result: p10 1.000, median 1.031, p90 1.062, P(<=1.04) = 0.645. I report 0.62 to allow for GPU-only risks the model does not capture.
forecasts.tokens: Main training about 5.2B tokens (p10 3.6B, p90 7.0B), single epoch over the 6.44B-token stream (base + C4 shards 1-36). That is about 4.4 h of H100 SXM at about 330k tok/s (p10 240k, p90 430k), starting about 64 min into the pod (55-75). The LR sweep (3x200M on base data) runs in parallel with the CPU data preparation and is not counted.

forecasts.method:
Method D: I split the test set by source and forecast each part from two independent anchors, then corrected for the extended contamination filter.

(1) What the data is. The base corpus is C4-en shard 0 plus WikiText-103 train (data/cache/lm/corpus/manifest.json, data/lm_corpus.py). By tokens, base train is 60% C4 (171.7 M) and 40% WikiText (113.1 M, 29,245 articles). The filtered test set (1,092 docs) is 59.0% C4 bytes and 41.0% WikiText bytes. All of it comes from the same hash split. The extra C4 shards 1-36 are a random partition of the same C4 release (assumed), so they are fresh, in-distribution data for the C4 part of the test set. They are not for the WikiText part.

(2) What the run actually reads. merge plus Stream (experiments/h100_data.py, h100_train.py) shuffles documents uniformly over about 6.44 B tokens and does not upweight base. At about 4.5 B trained tokens the run makes about 0.70 passes: each base document is seen at most once, about 30% of WikiText articles are never seen, and WikiText falls from 40% to 1.76% of training tokens (about 80 M wiki tokens, against 240 M in the CPU run).

(3) Per-source baseline. I compared per-document bits of the CPU model against GPT-2 small. CPU model: C4 1.191, wiki 1.070. GPT-2: C4 1.072, wiki 0.990. The wiki/C4 ratio of our models falls with quality on the 60/40 mix (0.976, 0.936, 0.898). GPT-2, trained without Wikipedia, sits at 0.924. A C4-heavy model should sit at about 0.93-0.95. So diluting WikiText costs about 0.02-0.05 bpb on wiki documents at equal general quality, which is about 0.01-0.02 on the whole test set.

(4) Anchor A, scaling up the CPU run. Start from 1.141. Data scaling uses the measured slope at constant learning rate with context 1024 (about -0.04 bpb per doubling at the test level) as a power law with beta 0.28-0.37, giving about -0.08 for 0.6 B to 4.5 B tokens. Model size 59 M to 85 M body parameters (alpha about 0.34) gives -0.035 to -0.05. The batch size of 524 k against 8 k tokens costs +0.005 to +0.02 per token. Training at context 1024 from the start gives -0.005. The C4-heavy mix against an unlimited supply of base-distribution data costs +0.00 to +0.01. Result: about 1.028 on the old filter list, as if uncontaminated.

(5) Anchor B, GPT-2 as reference. A 124 M llm.c model after 10 B FineWeb tokens beats OpenAI's GPT-2 checkpoint on FineWeb validation. I assume fast-v1 at about 4.5 B tokens with AdamW is roughly equal to llm.c at 6-9 B tokens. That puts the H100 model at about GPT-2 level (±2%) on in-domain C4, and at about 0.98-1.01 on WikiText. Result: about 1.02-1.035 on the extended document set.

(6) Extended filter. All 40 C4 documents excluded by the base list are short template or commercial pages (about 1 kB each). All 5 excluded wiki documents are explained by WikiText sister articles (RAAF area commands, Tucker-class destroyers, HMS Lion, Tom Johnson). The probe with one extra shard went from 45 to 58 excluded test documents. Extrapolating sublinearly (logarithmic to power-law) to 37 C4 shards gives about +60 to +130 more excluded documents, almost all short C4 template pages (about 50-130 kB, 1.4-3.6% of bytes). WikiText documents are essentially untouched.

These pages are hard for an uncontaminated model: GPT-2 scores about 1.3 on them. So GPT-2 re-scored on the extended set drops to about 1.027-1.037. The H100 model loses the near-duplicate bonus it would have had on them (about +0.006 against the old list). Against an uncontaminated-equivalent score, the extended set is about 0.003 easier.

(7) Counterfactual, the same compute on base data only (about 16 epochs). Following Muennighoff (R* about 15), the effective data would be about 3 B tokens (about 1.8 B effective for C4), and 124 M parameters on 285 M unique tokens is over-parameterised. Against that, the C4 mix wins by about 0.03 bpb (range 0.01-0.06): it gains about 0.03 on C4, which is 59% of the bytes, and loses at most about 0.01 on WikiText.

(8) Combining. I blended both anchors and added uncertainty in throughput and token count, plus a right-skewed tail for operational risk: learning rate, compile fallback, divergence, PCIe/NVL instead of SXM.

The 25 USD brake gives 6.23 pod-hours, minus the 30 min reserve and about 70 min of setup and sweep. That is about 0.70 passes over train_all (about 6.44 B tokens = 285 M base + about 36 x 171 M C4).
